description.zh-CN: 分级命令执行：可证明只读的命令免审批（shell_read，解析器证明层），其余白名单命令需审批（shell）；硬锁解释器/网络类
description.en-US: Tiered command execution: provably read-only commands run without approval (shell_read, parser proof layer), whitelisted ones need approval (shell); interpreters/network are hard-locked

tools.name: shell
tools.description: Run ONE whitelisted command and return {command, program, exit_code, success, timed_out, truncated, stdout, stderr}. Only a small allowlist is permitted (ls, cat, grep, git status; more via host config). Denylist: interpreter/wrapper/network commands (python, bash, curl, xargs, ...) are never allowed; high-risk user-judgeable commands (rm, sudo, chmod, ...) are refused unless the host unlock switch is on — they then still require user approval. Pipes, command substitution and shell metacharacters are rejected — pass a single simple command. Commands run WITHOUT a shell: the first word is spawned directly via PATH. On Windows hosts PATH usually resolves to Unix coreutils (Git's usr/bin) — use Unix-style commands; cmd builtins (dir, del, copy, `rmdir /s /q`) do not exist. For read-only work prefer `shell_read` (no approval needed).

command.description: single simple command, e.g. "git status"; no pipes/semicolons/backticks

cwd.description: optional working directory (absolute path, must exist)

tools.name: shell_read
tools.description: Run ONE PROVEN read-only command WITHOUT user approval: ls, cat, grep, or git status/log/diff/show. A proof layer parses the command (lexing + structure + semantics): it must be a single simple command — no unquoted pipes/redirection/`$()`/backticks/subshells, no `$` or backticks inside double quotes; no git global options (`-c`, `--git-dir`, ... can launch external programs via config); no write or external-program flags (`--output`, `--ext-diff`, `--textconv`); no credential paths (.env, .ssh, credentials, key material). Anything that cannot be PROVEN read-only is refused: re-run via the `shell` tool (asks the user) or pass a simpler command. Same result shape as `shell`. Paths must stay inside the allowed file roots (LOCOWRK_FS_ROOTS, default = app data root) — this includes the optional cwd argument; anything resolving outside is refused. Commands run WITHOUT a shell: the first word is spawned directly via PATH. On Windows hosts PATH usually resolves to Unix coreutils (Git's usr/bin) — use Unix-style commands; cmd builtins (dir, del, copy, `rmdir /s /q`) do not exist.

command.description: single simple command, e.g. "git status"; no pipes/semicolons/backticks

cwd.description: optional working directory (absolute path, must exist)
